full_judgment:
2. Prosecution case, in short, is that on 10-3-1996 at about 5-00-5-30 PM two minor boys, namely, Mizan and Faruque, aged about 8 years plucked wood apples from the tree belonging to deceased AKM Abdul Halim, Chairman of No. 8 Rajapur Union Parishad, Burichang. The eldest daughter of the deceased Abdul Halim, Chairman, Asma Akhtar Lipi, rebuked them over the said incident followed by an altercation between those two little boys and Lipi. Mizan and Faruque, thereafter, went to their respective homes and informed the incident to their relatives. Thereafter, the condemned prisoner Abul Kashem and the convict petitioner Anowar Hossain Pinto accompanied by other accused persons came to the house of the deceased Abdul Halim, Chairman in an aggressive mood and misbehaved with Lipi. Then Khorshed Alam, a domestic servant of Abdul Halim Chairman, persuaded them to stop and assured them that the Chairman would settle the matter after his return from Burichang. But the condemned prisoner, Abul Kashem and the accused appellant, Anowar Hossain Pinto started for Burichang without waiting for the arrival of the Chairman with dagger in their hands saying that they would demand justice from the Chairman on the way. At that time, the accused Nabalak Mia (since acquitted) called the condemned prisoner, Abul Kashem and accused appellant petitioner Anower Hossain to his house and instigated them by saying that if they could finish the Chairman on the way then the problem would be solved. Both the condemned prisoner, Abul Kashem and accused appellant, Anowar Hossain Pinto along with other accused persons then started for Burichang for committing the offence instigated by the accused Nabalak Mia. Meanwhile, Chairman Abdul Halim and PW 3 Mosharraf  Hossain, Member in one rickshaw and PW 2 Shamsul Huq, dealer in another rickshaw started for their village at about 7-00 PM on 10-3-1996 from Burichang and when they reached near the house of Shamsul Hoque, Member of Bares war village they got down from their rickshaw and started on foot. At about 8-00 PM, when all of them crossed the diversion road near the Ghungur river as the bridge on the said river was under construction and came to the pathway on the field, the condemned prisoner, Abul Kashem and accused appellant, Anowar Hossain Pinto came to them and informed the Chairman about the incident and demanded justice. Deceased Abdul Halim Chairman then told them that on reaching home he would settle the matter. But both the condemned prisoners and the accused appellant insisted that he must settle the matter then and there, which the deceased refused to do. As a result, the condemned prisoner Abul Kashem inflicted a dagger blow on the right side of chest of the deceased and then both of them fled away towards the wheat field. Both PWs 3 and 2 raised alarm and the neighbours came to the place of occurrence and heard narration of the occurrence. The deceased Chairman was then taken to the Burichang Hospital by rickshaw and the doctor on duty declared him dead. PW 1, Monowara Begum, wife of the deceased Chairman Abdul Halim, learnt about the occurrence, came to Burichang Hospital and learnt about the occurrence of murder from PW 2, Shamsul Hoque dealer and PW 3, Mosharaf Hossain Member. She went to Burichang Police Station and lodged a verbal ejahar at 11-15 PM on the date of the occurrence against the condemned prisoner, Abul Kashem and the accused appellant, Anowar Hossain Pinto only. PW 16, Officer-in-Charge of Burichang PS, Md Rezaul Karim recorded the FIR. He himself took up the investigation of the case and on completion of investigation submitted a charge sheet. 

 4. Prosecution in this case in all examined 16 witnesses. The accused persons were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and they declined to adduce any evidence. The defence plea as it appears from the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses and the examination of accused persons under section 342 of the CrPC is that they were innocent and they were falsely implicated in this case and the deceased must have been killed by dacoits. 

 7. The learned Additional Attorney-General submitted that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in omitting to consider that in the instant 'case the occurrence took place on 10-3-1996 at about 20-00 hours and first information report was lodged at 23-15 hours by PW 1, who narrated the chain of events which took place at her house on the said date and eventually culminated in the act of murder and later on gave a vivid description as to the mode and manner of attack on her deceased husband by the accused and inflicting of dagger blow as narrated to her by PWs 2 &3 and this earliest version of the case was duly established in the respective evidence of PW 1, PW 2 and PW 3 and corroborated by PW 4, PW 5, PW 7 and PW 8 and the case was proved beyond all reasonable doubt and non-consideration of such evidence resulted in miscarriage of justice. He next submitted that in the instant case an illegal and improper use was made of statements recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of PW 2 and PW 3 although such statements do not constitute substantive evidence and this is an illegality and caused miscarriage of justice. 

 10. It appears that so far as respondent No. 2, Abul Kashem is concerned, the prosecution case as narrated in the FIR has been well proved by the evidence of two eye witnesses, namely PWs 2 and 3. PW 2, Shamsul Huq deposed that both the informant and the accused persons are his neighbours and relatives and on 10th of March, 1996 at about 8-00 PM, the chairman was murdered. On that day in the evening PW 2 was coming by a rickshaw and chairman Abdul Halim and Mosharraf Member were coming by another rickshaw from Burichang. They got down from the rickshaw near the construction bridge over river Gungur, they crossed the diversion road and were proceeding through the pathway on the field when the accused Kashem and Pinto came there and stood in front of them and told chairman that there had been a "Golmal" in the house over plucking of wood apple and chairman was asked to do justice on the spot but chairman was insisting to go home and then adjudicating the matter when accused Kashem inflicted a dagger blow on the right side of the chest of chairman who cried and witness Mosharraf Hossain Member caught hold of Chairman. Accused Kashem and Pinto ran away towards the wheat filed. 

 14. It is true that such statement could be used by the accused for the purpose of cross-examining the witnesses. The only object in recording such statement is to obtain a hold over the witnesses but it does not establish that what they stated before the Magistrate is true. The High Court Division lost sight of the fact that the attention of the witness to such statement was not drawn as required under section 145 of the Evidence Act to specific statements and omissions. The High Court Division also did not consider that all omissions are not contradictions and in order to contradict the witness the specific part of the statements or omissions must be brought to the notice of the witness which was not done in the instant case. 

 21. Since this is not the rarest of the rare cases, ends of justice will be met if the sentence of death of the accused Kashem is converted into one of imprisonment for life. 

 "Let the convict-respondent, Anowar Hossain Pinto @ Anower Hossain be released to the satisfaction of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Comilla in connection with Death Reference No. 11 of 2000 and Criminal Appeal No. 1383 of 2000 arising out of Sessions Trial Case No. 37 of 1998 of the Court of Sessions Judge, Comilla corresponding to Burichang PS (Comilla) Case No. 6 of 1947 dated 10-3-1996 and be set at liberty forthwith."
